topic.subject: social
topic.title: Maps
topic.scope: physical, political and thematic maps, scale, directions, symbols, sketch and plan

misconceptions.statement: North is always 'up' on every map.
misconceptions.why: Students often associate the top of a page with the North direction due to standard wall map orientations.
misconceptions.fix: North is a geographic direction indicated by the compass rose or north arrow, not necessarily the top of the paper.

probe.question: If a map has the North arrow pointing to the left side of the page, which direction is at the top of the page?

misconceptions.statement: A symbol on a map is a literal picture of the object.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse pictorial representations with abstract symbols used in cartography.
misconceptions.fix: Symbols are standardized signs used to represent features like roads, temples, or bridges that are too small to be drawn to scale.

probe.question: Why is a small black dot used to represent a city on a map?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the city is actually a tiny black dot on the ground.

misconceptions.statement: A map with a larger area shown always has a larger scale.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the physical size of the map paper with the mathematical concept of scale ratio.
misconceptions.fix: Scale is the ratio between map distance and ground distance; a map covering a larger area actually has a smaller scale.

probe.question: Which map has a larger scale: a map of your school or a map of India?
probe.wrong_answer: The map of India because it is bigger.

misconceptions.statement: Political maps show the actual physical boundaries like mountains and rivers.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume that any line drawn on a map represents a physical feature.
misconceptions.fix: Political maps show man-made boundaries like states and countries, while physical maps show natural features like mountains and plateaus.

probe.question: Can you see the border between India and Pakistan if you are standing on the ground?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it is a physical line like a river or a mountain range.
